units.en: His grandfather Wang Zheng had served as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: His grandfather Zheng was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 裕亦目羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少。
units.en: For his part, Ruan Yu named Wang Xizhi, Wang Cheng, and Wang Yue the three outstanding younger men of the Wang family.
units.literal: Yu also regarded Xizhi with Wang Cheng and Wang Yue as the three young men of the Wang clan.

units.zh: 時東土饑荒，羲之輒開倉振貸。
units.en: Famine struck the eastern regions, and Wang Xizhi opened the government granaries to feed the people.
units.literal: At the time the eastern lands had famine; Xizhi then opened granaries and relieved with loans.

units.zh: 然朝廷賦役繁重，吳會憂甚，羲之每上疏爭之，事多見從。
units.en: Yet the court's taxes and labor demands remained crushing, and the Wu–Kuaiji area suffered acutely. Wang Xizhi repeatedly memorialized against the policy, and the throne often took his advice.
units.literal: Yet the court's levies and corvée were heavy and numerous; Wu and Hui were greatly worried; Xizhi often submitted memorials disputing them; affairs were mostly followed.

units.zh: 又遺尚書僕射謝安書曰：
units.en: He also wrote to Xie An, the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing:
units.literal: He also sent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie An a letter saying:

units.zh: 會稽有佳山水，名士多居之，謝安未仕時亦居焉。
units.en: Kuaiji boasted superb landscape, and celebrated gentlemen clustered there; Xie An had lived there too before he took office.
units.literal: Kuaiji has fine mountains and waters; famous scholars mostly dwell there; Xie An when not yet in office also dwelt there.

units.zh: 年五十九卒，贈金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: Wang Xizhi died at fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
units.literal: At age fifty-nine died; posthumously awarded Golden Purple Splendid Grand Master.

units.zh: 諸子遵父先旨，固讓不受。
units.en: His sons, obeying his earlier wishes, firmly declined the posthumous honor.
units.literal: The sons followed father's prior intent, firmly declined and did not accept.

units.zh: 嘗居山陰，夜雪初霽，月色清朗，四望皓然，獨酌酒詠左思《招隱詩》，忽憶戴逵。
units.en: While living in Shanyin he saw snow stop one night under a clear moon until the world gleamed white. He drank alone and recited Zuo Si's 《Summoning the Recluse》, and suddenly thought of Dai Kui.
units.literal: Once dwelt in Shanyin; night snow first cleared, moonlight clear bright, four views white; alone poured wine and chanted Zuo Si's "Summoning the Recluse Poems"; suddenly remembered Dai Kui.

units.zh: 逵時在剡，便夜乘小船詣之，經宿方至，造門不前而反。
units.en: Dai was in Shan county, so Huizhi took a boat by night; it took until the next morning to arrive, yet he turned back without crossing the threshold.
units.literal: Kui was then in Shan; then by night rode small boat went to him, after a night only arrived; reached gate did not advance but returned.

units.zh: 雅性放誕，好聲色，嘗夜與弟獻之共讀《高士傳贊》，獻之賞井丹高潔，徽之曰：「未若長卿慢世也。」
units.en: He was dissolute and fond of pleasure. One night he and his brother Xianzhi read the 《Eulogies to High-Minded Men》. Xianzhi admired Jing Dan's purity; Huizhi said, "He cannot match Sima Xiangru's contempt for the world."
units.literal: By nature unrestrained and wild, loved sound and color; once at night with younger brother Xianzhi together read 《Gaoshi Zhuan Zan》; Xianzhi praised Jing Dan's high purity; Huizhi said, "Not equal to Changqing's scorning the world."

units.zh: 後為黃門侍郎，棄官東歸，與獻之俱病篤，時有術人云：「人命應終，而有生人樂代者，則死者可生。」
units.en: He later served as a Palace Attendant, then quit and went east. He and Xianzhi both lay near death when an occultist said, "When a man's span is up, if another willingly trades his years, the dying man may live."
units.literal: Later became Palace Attendant, abandoned office and east returned; with Xianzhi both critically ill; at the time a technician said, "Human fate ought to end, but if there is a living person gladly to substitute, then the dead can live."

units.zh: 未幾，獻之卒，徽之奔喪不哭，直上靈床坐，取獻之琴彈之，久而不調，歎曰：「嗚呼子敬，人琴俱亡！」
units.en: Soon Xianzhi died. Huizhi hurried to the funeral but did not cry; he went straight to the bier, sat down, and took up Xianzhi's zither. The strings would not stay in tune. He cried, "O Zijing—the man is gone, and the instrument with him!"
units.literal: Before long, Xianzhi died; Huizhi rushed to mourning did not weep, straight ascended spirit couch sat, took Xianzhi's zither played it; long but not tuned; sighed saying, "Alas Zijing, person and zither both perished!"

units.zh: 先有背疾，遂潰裂，月餘亦卒。
units.en: An old abscess on his back broke open, and a little over a month later he too died.
units.literal: Earlier had back illness; then burst open; after a month more also died.

units.zh: 獻之怒曰：「遠慚荀奉倩，近愧劉真長。」
units.en: Xianzhi flared: "Compared with Xun Can in the past or Liu Tan among our own circle, I am ashamed."
units.literal: Xianzhi angrily said, "Far ashamed before Xun Fengqian, near ashamed before Liu Zhenchang."

units.zh: 七八歲時學書，羲之密從後掣其筆不得，歎曰：「此兒後當復有大名。」
units.en: At seven or eight, while practicing calligraphy, his father tried to tug the brush from behind and could not. Wang Xizhi sighed, "This boy will make a great name for himself."
units.literal: At seven or eight years studying writing, Xizhi secretly from behind pulled his brush but could not obtain; sighed saying, "This child later will again have great name."

units.zh: 嘗書壁為方丈大字，羲之甚以為能，觀者數百人。
units.en: He once brushed characters a full square foot high on a wall. His father was deeply impressed, and hundreds came to watch.
units.literal: Once wrote on wall as one zhang square large characters; Xizhi greatly thought him capable; viewers several hundred people.

units.zh: 桓溫嘗使書扇，筆誤落，因畫作烏駁牸牛，甚妙。
units.en: Huan Wen once asked him to write on a fan. The brush slipped, so he turned the blot into a dappled black cow—brilliantly done.
units.literal: Huan Wen once had him write on a fan; brush mistakenly dropped; therefore painted as dappled black cow, very subtle.

units.zh: 起家州主簿、秘書郎，轉丞，以選尚新安公主。
units.en: He began as a provincial chief clerk and Gentleman of the Palace Library, became an aide, and by imperial selection married the Princess of Xin'an.
units.literal: Rose from family as provincial chief clerk, Palace Secretary, transferred to aide; by selection married Princess of Xin'an.
